headline: Manny Pacquiao Returns to Government as National Anti-Poverty Commission Chief
seoTitle: Manny Pacquiao Named NAPC Chief, Joins Marcos Cabinet | FMB News
seoDescription: Manny Pacquiao has returned to government as secretary and lead convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission after taking his oath before President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
deck: Former senator Manny Pacquiao took his oath as secretary and lead convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission, a Cabinet-rank post that puts him in charge of coordinating the government's anti-poverty agenda.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Former senator and boxing champion Manny Pacquiao returned to government service on September 8 after taking his oath as secretary and lead convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission before President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Malacañang.

The Philippine News Agency, GMA News, Reuters, Inquirer and Philstar independently reported the appointment. Pacquiao succeeds Lope Santos III and assumes a position that carries Cabinet rank under the Social Reform and Poverty Alleviation Act.
As lead convenor, Pacquiao heads the NAPC secretariat and is responsible for coordinating government poverty-reduction efforts across national agencies, local governments and participating sectors.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The NAPC was created under Republic Act No. 8425 as the government's coordinating and advisory body for the Social Reform Agenda. Its mandate includes monitoring anti-poverty programs, recommending policy measures and ensuring that basic sectors participate in policymaking.

Pacquiao's appointment marks his first government post since his Senate term ended in 2022. He later ran for president that year and sought a Senate comeback in the 2025 midterm elections but did not win a seat.
The appointment also comes as the Marcos administration seeks to reduce poverty incidence further and has recently moved supervision of NAPC back under the Office of the President.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The NAPC role is not ceremonial. It sits at the center of how government agencies coordinate policies aimed at low-income communities, including questions of program overlap, targeting, resource allocation and participation by marginalized sectors.

Pacquiao enters the post with exceptional public visibility but will be judged on whether the commission can translate that visibility into measurable coordination and policy outcomes. The appointment therefore matters beyond his celebrity or political comeback.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The immediate test is the policy agenda Pacquiao sets for NAPC and how it aligns with the administration's broader poverty-reduction targets. Readers should watch for changes in program coordination, sector representation, budget priorities and measurable targets for the commission.
It will also be important to distinguish Pacquiao's NAPC responsibilities from other anti-poverty offices and advisers in government so that accountability for specific programs remains clear.

audit.socialCaption: Manny Pacquiao is back in government. The former senator has taken his oath as secretary and lead convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission, a Cabinet-rank role tasked with coordinating the country's anti-poverty agenda. FMB News explains what the post actually does and what to watch next.
verificationNotes: The central appointment and oath-taking are verified through PNA and GMA News reporting based on the Malacañang ceremony and the President's office announcement.
Reuters, Inquirer and Philstar independently corroborate Pacquiao's appointment, Cabinet rank and return to government service.
The article describes NAPC's mandate from Republic Act No. 8425 and official government reporting rather than inferring powers from the job title.
The story avoids treating Pacquiao's personal poverty narrative or future policy promises as proof of effectiveness; those claims are contextual rather than evidentiary.
Repository search found no existing FMB News article on Pacquiao's NAPC appointment, so the story is treated as an original report.
The hero and social crops are FMB-owned editorial graphics using the approved FMB icon and purple-violet/plum treatment and are explicitly not documentary photographs.
